jp: 私[わたし]は姉[あね]に古[ふる]い辞書[じしょ]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I received an old dictionary from my sister.
why: The speaker is the receiver and the giver is marked with に, so もらう fits; あげる would reverse the direction.

jp: 母[はは]に千円[せんえん]を{もらって|gv-morau}、パンを買[か]いに行[い]きました。
en: I got a thousand yen from my mother and went to buy bread.
why: I receive the money from my mother (に), so the receiving verb もらう is needed.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は祖父[そふ]に新[あたら]しい靴[くつ]を{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: My younger brother got new shoes from our grandfather.
why: The subject (弟) is the receiver and 祖父 is the giver, so it is もらう, not a giving verb.

jp: 隣[となり]のおばさんに、庭[にわ]でとれたみかんを{もらいました|gv-morau}。
en: I got some mandarin oranges from the lady next door that she had grown in her garden.
why: I am the receiver and the neighbour is the giver, so もらう is right.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]、叔母[おば]に使[つか]っていない洗濯機[せんたくき]を{もらう|gv-morau}予定[よてい]です。
en: Next month I am going to get a washing machine my aunt isn't using from her.
why: Receiving from my aunt (に) is もらう; the other verbs would make me the giver or need が for the giver.

jp: これは兄[あに]に{もらった|gv-morau}マグカップで、毎朝[まいあさ]使[つか]っています。
en: This is a mug I got from my older brother, and I use it every morning.
why: 兄に marks the giver, so the receiving verb もらった is needed; くれた would require 兄が.

jp: 毎月[まいつき]、母[はは]にお小遣[こづか]いを{もらっています|gv-morau}。
en: I get pocket money from my mother every month.
why: The speaker receives from 母, so もらう; the giving verbs reverse the direction or clash with に.
